span.p:
A decision surfaces during
the incident window

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Is it a technical
containment/eradication
step -- what to isolate,
when to eradicate?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Incident Commander decides.
Manager protects this person
from interruption -- Section 1.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Does it involve staffing,
budget, retainer/counsel,
or upward communication?

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Does it require legal
engagement -- privilege,
law enforcement, ransom
decision?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
SOC Manager and Legal
decide jointly -- Section 5.
CISO informed; Board
accountable on ransom calls.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
SOC Manager decides --
Sections 3 and 4.
Incident Commander is
consulted, never the one
fielding the call.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Check Figure 28.1's table
above -- if it isn't listed,
escalate to Part 25's
risk-acceptance framework.
